title: Henselianity descends through a quotient inside the maximal ideal
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring whose maximal-ideal pair is henselian in the idempotent-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Then the pair $(A/I,\mathfrak m/I)$ is henselian: for every finite $(A/I)$-algebra $B$, every idempotent of $B/(\mathfrak m/I)B$ lifts to a unique idempotent of $B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 09XK (label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753) applied to the surjection $A\to A/I$, as in the proof of (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of Lemma 0DYD (label lemma-henselian-henselian-pair, line 2785); with the definition in its finite-algebra form (characterization (3) of Lemma 09XI) in place of the integral form (4)

proof.text: Use the polynomial simple-root formulation of HenselianRing recorded by def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology. Since I is contained in the proper maximal ideal m, A/I is nontrivial and local. Surjectivity of the quotient map identifies the image of m with the maximal ideal of A/I, hence with its Jacobson radical. In Lean these are Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff, IsLocalRing.of_surjective', IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective, and IsLocalRing.jacobson_eq_maximalIdeal.

For a monic polynomial f over A/I and an approximate root b, choose a monic coefficient lift g over A using Polynomial.lifts_and_natDegree_eq_and_monic and a lift a0 of b. Evaluation commutes with the quotient map pi. The condition f(b) in pi(m) therefore says g(a0) belongs to pi^{-1}(pi(m)) = m + I = m. The same commutation holds for the derivative by Polynomial.derivative_map.

The derivative g'(a0) is a unit of A: otherwise localness places it in m, and its image in (A/I)/pi(m) is zero, contradicting the assumed unit condition for f'(b). Its image in A/m is consequently a unit. Apply HenselianRing.is_henselian for (A,m) to obtain a root a of g with a-a0 in m.

Project a to A/I. Commutation of evaluation gives f(pi(a)) = pi(g(a)) = 0, and pi(a)-b = pi(a-a0) belongs to pi(m). Together with the Jacobson-radical condition from step 1 this constructs HenselianRing (A/I) pi(m).

proof_origin.description: Direct polynomial root-lifting proof using the recorded HenselianRing predicate; replaces the finite-algebra idempotent route below the unit level.

Statement unchanged and checked (case I=m: A/I a field, pair (k,0), trivially henselian). Proof in three elementary steps: a finite A/I-algebra is finite over A through the surjection; (m/I)B = mB as ideals of B; the definition for (A,m) then gives unique idempotent lifting modulo (m/I)B. No new node needed: no integrality or finite-transitivity node is used because the surjection makes finiteness immediate.
